text.p: Base metal markets failed to excite during Tuesday afternoon LME trading, as earlier advances petered out, and by the end of the kerb prices were broadly steady.
In Chicago, the Commodities Research Bureau index fell 0.30 points to 246.04.

Copper did push up to $2,380 at one stage, against the background of the strike at Chile's Quebrada Blanca mine, but there was little followthrough, and the inevitable downturn followed. By the close, three months was back at an unchanged $2,360 a tonne, and seemingly set to remain a $2,320/2,380 jobbing market for the short-term. The cash/threes backwardation was little changed at $65/70.
Elsewhere, price rallies in aluminium and zinc similarly fizzled out, although both markets remained in the plus column.
Aluminium business was restricted to a tight range, but last trade was at $1,632 a tonne, up $8 from the close of last Friday.
Zinc prices remained firmer, although the market eased back from the highs near $1,290 to finish at $1,277, up $15.
Traders said the slippage from the highs reflected profit-taking once the short-covereing rally seen in the morning faded.
Nickel prices continued to trade in a narrow band, but edged up during the afternoon to close at $7,470, a $40 gain from pre-weekend levels.
Lead conditions were slow throughout, and the modest $3 advance to a closing $626 reflected the general trend.
Tin busuiness was also fairly slow, but the market held onto initial gains. Last trade was at $5,800, up $60.
Alloy did not move from the $1,500 level, with three months ending at $1,500/1,505 a tonne.

Signs of improvement in the condition of the U.S. wheat crop and heavy commodity fund sales caused CBOT wheat futures to end with moderate losses Tuesday, floor traders said. On Monday, the U.S. Department of Agriculture showed the condition of the hard red winter wheat crop--damaged by freezing spring temperatures--improving slightly. USDA showed modest improvement in the Kansas, Texas and Oklahoma crops. Wheat futures ended down 11-1/4 to two cents per bushel, with July down 8-3/4 at $4.02-1/2.

NYMEX gasoline prices eased Tuesday ahead of weekly oil inventory data which traders expected would show increasing gasoline supplies and give a bearish direction to a rangebound market. "The market seems to be waiting with bated breath for the API numbers, and if they come in as expected, the market could go much lower," said Mike De Luca, trader with Prudential Securities. June gasoline settled 0.23 cent lower at 60.31 cents a gallon. June crude ended up three cents a barrel at $19.66 though significantly off its session high of $19.84. June heating oil finished 0.48 cent a gallon higher at 53.53 cents.

COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended lower Tuesday, on moderate volumes, after an early rally in gold and silver failed to convincingly breach three week old resistance, amid talk of more European central bank activity, traders said. COMEX June gold ended down $2.80 an ounce at $341.50, after rallying to a session high early at $345.50 on light fund and bullion bank buying. In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $340.30/80, compared with the London Tuesday afternoon fix at $342.45 and the New York close Monday around $342.50/00.
